title: Exponents and Powers
description: Learn how exponents represent repeated multiplication and how to evaluate and simplify expressions using the laws of exponents, including zero and negative exponents, powers of powers, powers of products and quotients, fractional exponents, and scientific notation.

content.title: What Is an Exponent?
content.content: An exponent tells you how many times a number or expression is used as a factor in repeated multiplication. In the expression 3^4, the number 3 is multiplied by itself 4 times.
content.formula: a^n = a × a × a × ... × a (n factors)

content.title: Understanding an Exponent
content.question: What does 5^3 mean?
content.solution: The exponent 3 tells us to use 5 as a factor three times. Therefore, 5^3 = 5 × 5 × 5.

content.question: What does the exponent 4 mean in 7^4?
content.explanation: The exponent tells how many times the base is used as a factor. Thus, 7^4 = 7 × 7 × 7 × 7.

content.title: Base and Exponent
content.content: A power has two main parts: the base and the exponent. The base is the number or expression being multiplied, while the exponent tells how many times the base is used as a factor.

content.title: Identifying the Base and Exponent
content.question: Identify the base and exponent in 9^5.
content.solution: The number 9 is the base because it is being multiplied repeatedly. The number 5 is the exponent because it tells us how many times 9 is used as a factor.

content.question: In 4^6, what is the base?
content.explanation: The base is the number being repeatedly multiplied. In 4^6, the base is 4.

content.title: Writing Repeated Multiplication
content.content: Repeated multiplication can be written more compactly using exponents. Count how many times the same factor appears, then use that count as the exponent.

content.title: Writing a Product as a Power
content.question: Write 6 × 6 × 6 × 6 × 6 using an exponent.
content.solution: The factor 6 appears five times, so the exponent is 5.

content.question: Which power represents 3 × 3 × 3 × 3?
content.explanation: The factor 3 appears four times, so the expression is 3^4.

content.title: Evaluating Powers
content.content: To evaluate a power, rewrite it as repeated multiplication and then calculate the product.
content.formula: a^n = repeated multiplication of a, n times

content.title: Evaluating a Power
content.question: Evaluate 2^5.
content.solution: Rewrite the power as repeated multiplication: 2^5 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2. Multiplying gives 32.

content.title: Exponent of 0
content.content: Any nonzero number raised to the zero power equals 1. This rule is consistent with the quotient law for exponents because dividing a nonzero power by itself leaves 1.

content.title: Zero Exponent
content.question: Evaluate 12^0.
content.solution: Any nonzero number raised to the zero power equals 1.

content.title: Negative Exponents
content.content: A negative exponent indicates the reciprocal of the corresponding positive power. Move the base from the numerator to the denominator, or from the denominator to the numerator, and make the exponent positive.

content.title: Evaluating a Negative Exponent
content.question: Rewrite 2^(-3) using a positive exponent.
content.solution: Move 2 to the denominator and change the exponent from -3 to 3. Thus, 2^(-3) = 1/2^3 = 1/8.

content.title: Product of Powers
content.content: When multiplying powers with the same nonzero base, keep the common base and add the exponents.

content.title: Multiplying Powers
content.question: Simplify x^3 × x^5.
content.solution: The bases are the same, so add the exponents: x^(3+5) = x^8.

content.question: Simplify 2^4 × 2^3.
content.explanation: When multiplying powers with the same base, add the exponents: 2^4 × 2^3 = 2^(4+3) = 2^7.

content.title: Quotient of Powers
content.content: When dividing powers with the same nonzero base, keep the common base and subtract the exponent in the denominator from the exponent in the numerator.

content.question: Simplify 3^8 / 3^5.
content.explanation: For a quotient with the same base, subtract the exponents: 3^(8-5) = 3^3.

content.title: Power of a Power
content.content: When a power is raised to another power, keep the base and multiply the exponents.

content.title: Power of a Product
content.content: When a product is raised to a power, the exponent applies to every factor inside the parentheses.

content.title: Power of a Product
content.question: Simplify (3x)^4.
content.solution: Apply the exponent to both 3 and x: (3x)^4 = 3^4x^4 = 81x^4.

content.title: Power of a Quotient
content.content: When a quotient is raised to a power, the exponent applies to both the numerator and denominator.

content.title: Power of a Quotient
content.question: Simplify (x/3)^2.
content.solution: Apply the exponent to both the numerator and denominator: (x/3)^2 = x^2/3^2 = x^2/9.

content.title: Negative and Fractional Exponents
content.content: A negative exponent represents a reciprocal, while a fractional exponent represents a root. The denominator of the fractional exponent indicates the root, and the numerator indicates the power.
content.formula: a^(1/n) = nth root of a; a^(m/n) = nth root of (a^m)

content.title: Fractional Exponent
content.question: Evaluate 16^(1/2).
content.solution: A power of 1/2 represents a square root. Therefore, 16^(1/2) = √16 = 4.

content.question: What does 27^(1/3) represent?
content.explanation: The denominator 3 indicates a cube root, so 27^(1/3) = ∛27 = 3.

content.title: Scientific Notation
content.content: Scientific notation is a way to write very large or very small numbers using a number between 1 and 10 multiplied by a power of 10. The exponent tells how many places the decimal point moves.

content.title: Writing Scientific Notation
content.question: Write 4500000 in scientific notation.
content.solution: Move the decimal point six places to the left to obtain 4.5. Therefore, 4500000 = 4.5 × 10^6.

content.question: Which is the scientific notation of 0.00032?
content.explanation: The decimal moves four places to the right to become 3.2, so the exponent is -4: 0.00032 = 3.2 × 10^-4.

content.title: Applying Exponent Rules
content.content: Exponent rules can be combined when simplifying expressions. First identify the structure of the expression, then apply the appropriate rule. Keep track of signs, parentheses, and whether the bases are actually the same.
content.formula: a^m × a^n = a^(m+n); a^m/a^n = a^(m-n); (a^m)^n = a^(mn); (ab)^n = a^n b^n; (a/b)^n = a^n/b^n

content.title: Combining Exponent Rules
content.question: Simplify (x^2)^3 × x^4.
content.solution: First apply the power-of-a-power rule: (x^2)^3 = x^6. Then multiply powers with the same base: x^6 × x^4 = x^10.

content.question: Simplify (a^2)^3 × a^4.
content.explanation: First, (a^2)^3 = a^6. Then a^6 × a^4 = a^10 by adding the exponents.
